name: Shafiur Rahman
contribution: Shafiur Rahman (1918–1952) was a government employee and language-rights supporter killed by police fire on Nawabpur Road in Dhaka on 22 February 1952, during the mourning demonstrations that followed the Language Movement killings of 21 February.
context: The Language Movement had grown from demands for Bangla's recognition in public and state life. Rahman's death showed that the repression of the movement reached beyond university students: ordinary workers and residents joining or caught in public demonstrations also became part of the movement's martyr history.
impact: Rahman's memory expanded the social meaning of Ekushey beyond a single day's student protest. Through annual commemoration, Shaheed Minar remembrance, and the international language-rights legacy associated with 21 February, his name remains part of Bangladesh's public history of cultural dignity and state violence.
highlight: Language Movement martyr killed on Nawabpur Road during the 22 February 1952 mourning procession.
seoTitle: Shafiur Rahman: Language Movement Martyr of 22 February 1952
seoDescription: Learn about Shafiur Rahman (1918–1952), the language-movement martyr killed on Dhaka's Nawabpur Road on 22 February 1952 and remembered in Bangladesh's Ekushey tradition.
shortAnswer: Shafiur Rahman was a government employee killed by police fire on 22 February 1952 during Language Movement demonstrations in Dhaka, and is remembered as a language martyr.

faq.question: Who was Shafiur Rahman?
faq.answer: Shafiur Rahman was a government employee and language-rights supporter who was killed by police fire on Nawabpur Road in Dhaka on 22 February 1952. He is remembered as a martyr of the Language Movement.

faq.question: Why is Shafiur Rahman remembered on Ekushey?
faq.answer: His death during the 22 February mourning demonstrations broadened the movement's martyr memory beyond the 21 February student killings and became part of the annual Shaheed Minar and language-rights tradition.
